records.nativeDetailObservation: Original file inspected again with detail=original, preserving2752x1536 in final sighting.
concreteImageFindings: The two-column original correctly distinguishes the copper reducing assay from the enzymatic GOD/POD glucose assay. Blue Cu(II) solution, warming, red Cu(I)-oxide precipitate and the peroxide-coupled color signal support that comparison.

The exact lower negative caption reads: Bleibt blau (Negativ: kein reduzierender Zucker). It turns a negative method result into unqualified absence of reducing sugar. A concentration below method sensitivity or a method/matrix limitation can produce non-detection without literal zero. The unchanged cases explicitly teach analytical limits; the new goal description now emphasizes analytical scope. No qualifying closed model or detection-limit statement accompanies this caption.

The scientific correction needed is narrow: express non-detection under the method conditions rather than absolute absence. Existing layout, color contrast, the useful specificity comparison, raster bytes and format are not altered by this review.

At316px image width, detailed captions/equations are small; the overall two-column signal contrast remains visible. At636px, the negative wording and most details are readable. The substantive REVISE is the absence claim, independent of text density or image generator.

PODSpecificAdditionalFinding.actualPixels: H2O2 + Peroxidase (POD) + Farbstoff -> Farbiges Signal + H2O
PODSpecificAdditionalFinding.reason: In these actual pixels this is an unbalanced schematic reagent-to-signal sequence. Farbiges Signal is not a named chemical product species, and no enzyme count, balanced stoichiometry, disappearing-enzyme graphic or explicit enzyme-consumption statement is present. POD involvement in peroxide-coupled color generation is clear. This notation would be unsuitable as a stoichiometric reaction equation, but the qualitative orientation diagram does not establish enzyme consumption.
PODSpecificAdditionalFinding.scope: Independent own interpretation of the same original-resolution image; no second expected verdict, pixel edit or full mechanistic approval.

resourceLinks.description: Comicartiger Vergleich der enzymatischen Lactosespaltung mit und ohne Lactase. Die Darmsymbole stehen allgemein für den Verdauungstrakt; die Abbildung ist kein anatomischer Lageplan oder klinischer Befund.
resourceLinks.altText: Mit Lactase wird die schematische Lactose in zwei Einfachzucker gespalten; ohne Lactase bleibt sie verbunden. Darmsymbole veranschaulichen den Verdauungstrakt.

concreteImageFindings: The upper lane shows linked lactose reaching a green enzyme pocket, then two separated sugar pieces. The lower lane lacks lactase and carries the joined pair onward. Labels and color differences remain clear in both native and316/636px raster views.

Both general intestine icons are digestive-tract context. No intestinal-wall crossing, villus transport arrow, clinical location or mechanism of absorption is drawn. The good hydrolysis illustration does not claim to demonstrate the entire absorption goal.

The new English intestinal absorption wording remains compatible with the broader whole-goal context; it does not turn the icon into an anatomical map or diagnostic evidence. A binary with/without-lactase model is an orientation simplification, not a numerical individual lactase-activity measurement.
